items.item_text: Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in education, counseling, or student affairs.

Responsible for onboarding of reentry students into the School of Social Sciences, Humanities and Arts (SSHA), including but not limited to reentry activities, processes, events, and programs. Researches, develops, plans, and executes School activities & initiatives for reentry and returning students, including but not limited to SSHA DCP Reentry Open House, Coffee and Tea at the TRV, mandatory reentry meetings, and other reentry initiatives. Oversees other Degree Completion Program programs and processes. Provides student services support to traditional transfer students alongside the Academic Advisor, Transfer Coordinator.

Provides advice and assistance to students on all aspects of their academic experience, including progression and requirement matters, 2-3 faculty department/School/campus-wide General Education. Identifies students with GPA or progress problems, advises students, and recommends appropriate courses of action by the department/School (e.g., academic probation, dismissal, Normal Progress Policy). Determines barriers, distractions, and complications affecting students' academic success, helps students recognize these key nonacademic issues, and makes appropriate referrals for additional therapeutic counseling and/or assistance from other units. Advises students on a wide range of course possibilities and/or ways to complete degree requirements that may not be clearly defined. Confirms that students have met requirements for degree completion when there are no clear precedents or articulations, such as interdisciplinary programs, or when transfer work is involved.

Advises new and continuing instructors on departmental/School and/or university requirements and student advising issues. Provides faculty referrals to the appropriate offices, including the Office of Student Conduct and the Dean of Students Office. Advises new and continuing instructors on major, School, and university policies and procedures. Assists faculty in determining course scheduling needs for student progression to graduation. Participates in planning academic curriculum in collaboration with the chair and faculty, and with other departments, to ensure students' progress through course sequences, avoid conflicts, and ensure compliance with organization-wide policies.
Collaborates with other Degree Completion Program partners/colleagues across the UC Merced campus and amongst the University of California Reengagement Consortium (UCRC).
Other duties as assigned. Includes responding to other unanticipated advising support questions, inquiries, and needs. May supervise student employees.
Advanced degree in education, counseling, or student affairs. (Preferred)
